about: Berättelser efter striden (Listen to the story). Byggs av prototypes/story-listen/export.py, ändra inte för hand.

stories.title: The cat and the bird
lines: The {sun} is up.
A {cat} sits under a {tree}.
A {bird} sings in the tree, and the cat looks up.

stories.title: The dog and the map
lines: A {dog} finds a {map}.
The map shows a {tree} and a {flower}.
The dog runs to the tree, and there is the flower!

stories.title: Breakfast at the brook
lines: The {bear} eats {breakfast} by the {water}.
It has an {apple} and a {fish}.
A {frog} jumps into the water. Splash!

stories.title: The duck and the sword
lines: A {duck} swims in the {water}.
It finds a {sword} in the water.
"Look!" says the duck to the {frog}. "I have a sword!"

stories.title: Under the big oak
lines: Under the {big} oak, a {mouse} eats {porridge}.
A {bee} comes and sits on a {leaf}.
The mouse gives the bee some porridge.

stories.title: The fox and the key
lines: The {fox} has a {key} and a {shield}.
The key opens a hole in the {tree}.
Inside, there is an {apple} for the fox!

stories.title: Morning at the farm
lines: It is morning at the farm.
The {cow} and the {horse} play in the {sun}.
The {pig} finds {one} egg, then {two} more!
Now there are {three} eggs, and one {egg} is very {small}.

stories.title: Bedtime at the farm
lines: It is late, and the {small dog|small_dog} is tired.
"Time to {go to bed|go_to_bed}!" says the {horse}.
But the {big dog|big_dog} wants to play with the {pig}.
"Are you my {enemy}?" says the pig. "No, I am your friend!" says the dog.
"No! Go to bed!" says the {cow}.

stories.title: The rain
lines: The {rain} comes, and the {fox} runs to its {house}.
But a {snake} is in the house!
They do not want a {battle}, so they sit by the {fire}.
Now they are friends.

stories.title: Before bed
lines: "I {brush my teeth|brush_my_teeth}," says the {bear}.
Then it can {jump} into bed.
But a {mouse} is in the bed!
The bear and the mouse jump, and they {run} out of the {house}.

stories.title: The bird nest
lines: A {bird} has a {nest} in a tree.
In the nest, there are {four} eggs, and then one more. Now there are {five}!
At night, the bird looks at a {star} in the sky.
In the morning, the eggs open, and the bird is very {happy}.

stories.title: The first day at school
lines: Today the {dog} goes to {school}.
At school, the {cat} and the dog {eat} apples.
Then they {sleep} under a {tree}.
The dog is {happy}. School is fun!

stories.title: The dark forest
lines: The {forest} is dark, and the {fox} is {sad}.
It cannot find its {house}.
Then a {fish} in the water says, "Swim with me!"
The fox can {swim}, and it swims very {fast} to its house.

stories.title: The fast frog
lines: The {frog} is {fast}, but the {duck} is not.
They {swim} to the other side of the {water}.
The frog wins, but the duck is {sad}.
So the frog gives the duck an {apple}.

stories.title: The owl tree
lines: At night, the {moon} is big.
An {owl} and a {bat} sit in a {tree}.
"I can {jump high|jump_high}," says the bat.
"I can see in the dark," says the owl.

stories.title: The slow troll
lines: The {troll} wants to {walk the dog|walk_the_dog}.
But the troll is very {slow}.
The {dog} wants to {run fast|run_fast}!
So the dog pulls, and the troll runs too.

stories.title: The troll forgets
lines: "I forget everything!" says the troll.
"Where is my {map}? Where is my {key}?"
A {bird} finds the map under a {tree}.
A {mouse} finds the key in the {porridge}!
Now the troll can find its {house} in the {forest}.
"Thank you!" says the troll, and it is very {happy}.

stories.title: The camel at the oasis
lines: The {sun} is up, and the {camel} walks to the {water}.
It finds a {cup} by a {tree}.
There is no {milk} in the cup, only {juice}.
So the camel eats some {bread} and a {banana}.
In the evening, the camel and its friend {watch TV|watch_tv} in the {house}.

stories.title: Breakfast at the oasis
lines: One morning, you eat {breakfast} by the {water}.
There is {bread}, an {egg}, a {banana}, and a {cup} of {milk}.
Then a {camel} comes, and it eats your banana!
You are {sad}, but the camel has some {juice} for you.
Now you are {happy}, and the camel is happy too.

stories.title: The caravan stops
lines: It is a {hot} day in the desert.
The caravan stops, and the camels sit by the {water}.
The children {play football|play_football} in the sand.
Then everyone eats {cake}, and the {juice} is nice and {cold}.
The {camel} eats an {orange}.

stories.title: The camel's lunch
lines: It is lunch time for the {camel}.
It eats a {carrot} and an {orange}.
But it does not eat the {cheese}.
The cheese sits in the {sun} all day, and now it is {hot}!
Then a {mouse} comes and eats it all.

stories.title: The wind takes your hat
lines: You walk up a big sand dune in a {hat}.
The hat is {new}, but the wind takes it, and it flies away!
You {run} after it, and you lose a {shoe} and a {sock}.
At the top, you find an {old} hat, but it is not your hat.
So you take a {T-shirt|shirt} from your {bag} and put it on your head, because the {sun} is hot.
You put on some {pants} too, and now you look very funny.

stories.title: The fox and the old shoe
lines: The {fox} finds an {old shoe|old_shoe} in the sand.
"This is my {hat}, and it is {new}!" says the fox.
It puts the shoe on its head and walks to the {camel}.
The camel laughs. "That is not a hat. It is a {shoe}!"
So the camel gives the fox a real {hat} from its {bag}.

stories.title: Shopping with coins
lines: Today you go to the market with {six} coins.
You want a {pizza}, an {ice cream|ice_cream}, and a {cookie}.
The pizza costs {five} coins, so you buy it.
Now you have one {coin}. That is not enough for the ice cream.
But the man at the market gives you a {cookie} for free!

stories.title: The bear at the market
lines: A {bear} comes to the market with {seven} coins.
"I want a {tomato}," says the bear.
But then it sees the {ice cream|ice_cream}, and it wants that too.
The bear buys a tomato and an ice cream, and it is very {happy}.
At home, the bear and its friend {play video games|play_video_games}.

stories.title: Night at the camp
lines: It is night at the camp, and the {moon} is up.
The {clock} says it is time to {sleep}.
You go into your {tent}.
But a {cat} is {in} your {bed}!
So you sleep on a {chair}, and you dream that you {go skiing|go_skiing}.

stories.title: Where is my chair?
lines: "Where is my {chair}?" says the {camel}.
It is not {in} the {tent}.
It is not by the {bed}, and it is not by the {clock}.
The camel looks {in} its {bag}, but a chair is too big for a bag!
Then the camel goes out, and there is the chair. A {bear} sits on it in the {sun}!

stories.title: Picnic by the cactus
lines: You sit by a big {cactus}, and you are very {hungry}.
You have a {plate}, a {spoon}, and a {knife}.
But there is no food! You forgot it at home.
You are {thirsty} too, and there is no {water}.
Then a {camel} comes with {bread}, some {cheese}, and some {juice}.

stories.title: The money in the cactus
lines: The {camel} has some {money} in a {bag}.
It walks by a {cactus}, and the bag gets a hole.
The money falls out, and the camel does not see it.
Now the camel is {hungry}, but it cannot buy {bread}.
Then a {mouse} brings back the money on a {plate}!

stories.title: The ball in the ruin
lines: You kick a {ball}, and it goes into an {old} ruin.
You open the {door} and look for it.
Is the ball {under} the {box}? No.
Is it {on} the {book}? No.
It is {under} the {window}, next to a {cat}!

stories.title: The old book
lines: In the ruin, a {book} is {on} a {box}.
It is very {old}.
A {key} is {under} the book.
The key opens the {door}, and you go in.
In the room, there is a big {window} and a red {ball}.

stories.title: Counting at the gate
lines: At the Sun Gate, there are {eight} cars and {nine} boats.
A {lion} sits {on} a {car}.
"This is my car!" says the lion.
"No, it is my car!" says a {camel}.
So they count to {ten} and drive away in the car together.

stories.title: The lion's boat
lines: The {lion} wants to go on the water in a {boat}.
It has {ten} coins.
A {boat} costs {nine} coins, and a {car} costs {eight}.
The lion buys the boat, and it has one coin left.
"This is a good day," says the lion, and it is very {happy}.

stories.title: The Sphinx's story
lines: "Listen to my story," says the Sphinx.
A {camel} walks to the oasis and drinks {milk} from a {cup}.
At the market, it buys a {pizza} with {seven} coins.
At night, it sleeps {in} a {tent}, and the {clock} goes tick, tock.
In the morning, it finds a {ball} under a {box} in the ruin.
Then it puts on a {hat} and drives a {car} to the Sun Gate.
"Now you know my story," says the Sphinx. "Are you {happy}?"

stories.title: The dock
lines: You {walk} to the dock with your {dog}.
"Please {stop}!" says a {frog}.
"There is a {mushroom} by your {foot}."
You pick it up with your {hand}, and the frog says, "Thank you!"

stories.title: The bear in the boat
lines: A {boat} comes to the dock.
A {bear} gets out and starts to {walk}.
It has a {mushroom} in each {hand}.
"Come here!" says the bear. "Let us cook them!"

stories.title: The lily pond
lines: A {frog} sits on a {leaf} in the pond.
It can {look} at the fish with one {eye}.
You {wave} to the frog, and it starts to {clap}!
Then it jumps into the {water}.

stories.title: Muddy hands
lines: You play in the mud, and now your {hand} is black.
"Look at your hands!" says the {owl}.
"I {wash my hands|wash_my_hands}," you say.
Then you {clap}, and the owl puts a wing to its {ear}. "Too loud!"

stories.title: The misty glade
lines: In the mist, a small {troll} starts to {cry}.
"I cannot see my {nose}!" it says.
You {sit} with the troll, and you wait.
The sun comes out, and the troll can {smile} again.

stories.title: The funny bear
lines: The {bear} wants to make you {laugh}.
It puts an {apple} on its {nose}.
Then it puts a {banana} in its {mouth}.
You laugh, and the bear tries to {stand} on one {foot}!

stories.title: Homework
lines: After school, you {do homework|do_homework}.
You take a {pencil} and some {paper}.
You {write} your name, and then you {draw} a big fish.
Now you can {read a book|read_a_book}.

stories.title: The mouse draws a cat
lines: A {mouse} wants to {draw a cat|draw_a_cat}.
It draws the cat on the {paper} with a {pencil}.
But the cat looks very real!
The mouse runs under the {bed}, and next time it will {draw a dog|draw_a_dog}.

stories.title: The frog stone
lines: On the big stone, the frogs {sing}.
"Come and {dance}!" they say.
You {climb} up on the stone.
You {listen to music|listen_to_music} with the frogs all night.

stories.title: Music in the trees
lines: You {ride a bike|ride_a_bike} to the swamp.
There is {music} in the trees.
A {bird} can {sing}, and a {bear} can {dance}!
You stop your bike, and you {dance} too.

stories.title: The witch hut
lines: The {witch} lives in a little hut.
She wants to {cook} soup with a {carrot} and a {mushroom}.
But the hut is a mess. "First I {clean my room|clean_my_room}," she says.
Then she can {give} you some soup.

stories.title: Shower time
lines: The {pig} plays in the mud all day.
"Now you must {take a shower|take_a_shower}!" says the {witch}.
The pig sings in the shower.
Then the witch can {give} the pig a {cookie}.

stories.title: The bear's tooth
lines: At night, the fireflies come out in the meadow.
A {bear} cannot sleep, because its {tooth} hurts.
It sits down and starts to {think}.
"I know!" it says. "I {brush my teeth|brush_my_teeth}!"
Now the bear can {sleep}.

stories.title: Long legs
lines: A {frog} and a {bird} play in the meadow.
"Look at my {leg}!" says the frog. "I can {jump high|jump_high}!"
"Look at my wing!" says the bird. "It is like an {arm}!"
"I {think} we are both very good," they say.

stories.title: The root cave
lines: You and your {dog} walk into the root cave.
It is dark, so you {wait} by the door.
Then a small {bat} comes and says, "Hello!"
It is not scary. You give the bat a {hug}.

stories.title: Wait for me
lines: "Today we go to the swamp!" says the {cat}.
"Please {wait}!" says the {dog}. "I am not dressed now."
The dog puts on a {hat} and a {T-shirt|shirt}.
Then the dog and the cat {hug}, and they go.

stories.title: The witch who mumbles
lines: The {witch} mumbles all day.
"Mmm, mmm," she says, and nobody knows what she wants.
The {frog} puts its {ear} near her {mouth}.
"She wants to {sing}!" says the frog.
So the {bear} plays {music}, and the witch starts to {dance}.
Now she does not mumble, and she can {smile}.
"Thank you," she says, and she gives everyone a big {hug}.
